questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution

**Working.**

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A catalytic oxidizer processes $10\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$ of air at $1200\,\text{mg/m}^3$ VOC with $97\%$ destruction. The mass of VOC destroyed per hour is _____ kg.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Mass destroyed = Q × C × η, converted to kg/h.

**Working.**
$$10 \times 1200 \times 0.97 = 11{,}640\,\text{mg/s} = 11.64\,\text{g/s} = 41.904\,\text{kg/h}.$$
Wait—recalculate: $10 \times 1200 = 12{,}000\,\text{mg/s}$, times $0.97 = 11{,}640\,\text{mg/s} = 11.64\,\text{g/s} = 41.904\,\text{kg/h}$.
Hmm, that's 41.904. Let me re-read: $1200\,\text{mg/m}^3 \times 10\,\text{m}^3/\text{s} = 12{,}000\,\text{mg/s}$. $12{,}000 \times 0.97 = 11{,}640\,\text{mg/s} = 11.64\,\text{g/s}$. $11.64 \times 3600 / 1000 = 41.904\,\text{kg/h}$.

**Answer.** $41.90\,\text{kg/h}$

questions.stem: An activated carbon bed adsorber has a capacity of $0.3\,\text{kg VOC/kg carbon}$. With $500\,\text{kg}$ of carbon and treating a stream at $50\,\text{g/m}^3$ at $2\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$, the breakthrough time is _____ hours.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Total capacity = bed mass × adsorption capacity. Flow rate of VOC = Q × C. Time = capacity / flow.

**Working.**
$$\text{Capacity} = 500 \times 0.3 = 150\,\text{kg VOC}.$$
$$\text{Flow} = 2 \times 50 = 100\,\text{g/s} = 0.1\,\text{kg/s}.$$
$$t = 150 / 0.1 = 1500\,\text{s} = 41.67\,\text{h}.$$

**Answer.** $41.67\,\text{h}$

NH₃ and SO₂ in cold temperatures

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: The rate constant for the reaction NO₂ + hν → NO + O is $k = 0.005\,\text{min}^{-1}$. If initial NO₂ concentration is $100\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$, the concentration after $60\,\text{min}$ of sunlight is _____ $\mu\text{g/m}^3$ (to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** First-order decay: $C = C_0 e^{-kt}$.

**Working.**
$$C = 100 \times e^{-0.005 \times 60} = 100 \times e^{-0.3} = 100 \times 0.7408 = 74.1.$$

**Answer.** $74.1\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$

questions.stem: A CEMS measures SO₂ at $350\,\text{ppm}$ (dry basis) with $12\%$ O₂ in the flue gas. The emission corrected to $3\%$ O₂ is _____ ppm (to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Corrected concentration = measured × (20.9 − 3) / (20.9 − measured O₂).

**Working.**
$$350 \times (20.9 - 3) / (20.9 - 12) = 350 \times 17.9 / 8.9 = 350 \times 2.0112 = 704.0.$$
Wait—recheck: correction formula for O₂ is: $C_{\text{corr}} = C_{\text{meas}} \times \frac{20.9 - \text{O}_{2,\text{ref}}}{20.9 - \text{O}_{2,\text{meas}}}$.
$$C_{\text{corr}} = 350 \times \frac{20.9 - 3}{20.9 - 12} = 350 \times \frac{17.9}{8.9} = 350 \times 2.0112 = 704.0.$$

**Answer.** $704.0\,\text{ppm}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A CEMS measures particulate at $45\,\text{mg/Nm}^3$ with $6\%$ O₂. Corrected to $3\%$ O₂, the value is _____ $\text{mg/Nm}^3$ (to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $C_{\text{corr}} = C_{\text{meas}} \times \frac{20.9 - \text{O}_{2,\text{ref}}}{20.9 - \text{O}_{2,\text{meas}}}$.

**Working.**
$$45 \times \frac{20.9 - 3}{20.9 - 6} = 45 \times \frac{17.9}{14.9} = 45 \times 1.2013 = 54.1.$$
Wait—recompute: $17.9/14.9 = 1.20134$, times $45 = 54.06 \approx 54.1$.

**Answer.** $54.1\,\text{mg/Nm}^3$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A CEMS reports CO at $200\,\text{ppm}$. The regulatory limit is $500\,\text{ppm}$ (corrected to $3\%$ O₂). If measured O₂ is $8\%$, the corrected CO is _____ ppm. Is it within limit? (Answer 1 for yes, 0 for no).

Let me recalculate more carefully: $17.9/12.9 = 1.387597$, $\times 200 = 277.52$.

**Answer.** $277.5\,\text{ppm}$, within limit

questions.stem: The Fresnel number for a barrier is $N = \frac{2\delta}{\lambda}$, where $\delta$ is the path difference and $\lambda$ is the wavelength. If $\delta = 1.5\,\text{m}$ and the frequency is $500\,\text{Hz}$ (speed of sound $c = 343\,\text{m/s}$), the Fresnel number is _____ (to 1 decimal place).

**Answer.** 4.67

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A baghouse filters $15\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$ of air. The air-to-cloth ratio is $1.5\,\text{m/min}$. The required filter area is _____ $\text{m}^2$.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Air-to-cloth ratio = Q / A. $A = Q / \text{ratio}$.

**Working.**
$$Q = 15\,\text{m}^3/\text{s} = 900\,\text{m}^3/\text{min}.$$
$$A = 900 / 1.5 = 600\,\text{m}^2.$$

**Answer.** $600\,\text{m}^2$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A venturi scrubber operates at a pressure drop of $1500\,\text{Pa}$. The overall collection efficiency for $1\,\mu\text{m}$ particles is approximately _____ $\%$ (use $\eta = 1 - e^{-0.002 \Delta P}$, with $\Delta P$ in Pa).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Empirical venturi scrubber efficiency model.

**Working.**
$$\eta = 1 - e^{-0.002 \times 1500} = 1 - e^{-3} = 1 - 0.0498 = 0.9502 = 95.0\%.$$

**Answer.** $95.0\%$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: Which device has the highest collection efficiency for PM₂.₅?
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Baghouses achieve >99% for fine particles including PM₂.₅.

**Working.**
Fabric filters are the gold standard for fine particulate.

**Answer.** Fabric filter (baghouse)

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A multi-cyclone has $20$ small tubes. The overall collection efficiency is $85\%$. If one tube is bypassed (1/20 of flow), the overall efficiency drops to _____ $\%$.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Bypassed fraction carries 100% of particles. Overall η = η_active × fraction_active + fraction_bypassed.

**Working.**
$$\eta = 0.85 \times (19/20) + 1.0 \times (1/20) = 0.85 \times 0.95 + 0.05 = 0.8075 + 0.05 = 0.8575.$$
Wait—that's wrong. Let me reconsider: if one tube is bypassed, the flow through it has 0% efficiency.
$$\eta = 0.85 \times (19/20) + 0 \times (1/20) = 0.8075 = 80.75\%.$$

**Answer.** $80.75\%$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: An ESP has a drift velocity of $0.1\,\text{m/s}$ and collecting area $A = 400\,\text{m}^2$. The gas flow rate is $10\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$. The Deutsch–Anderson efficiency is _____ $\%$ (to 2 decimal places).

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: The dry adiabatic lapse rate (DALR) is approximately $9.8\,^\circ\text{C/km}$. If the ground temperature is $25^\circ\text{C}$, the temperature at $2\,\text{km}$ altitude following a dry adiabat is _____ $^\circ\text{C}$.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $T = T_0 - \text{DALR} \times z$.

**Working.**
$$25 - 9.8 \times 2 = 25 - 19.6 = 5.4.$$

**Answer.** $5.4^\circ\text{C}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: The mixing height determines the volume available for pollutant dispersion. If the mixing height is $800\,\text{m}$ and wind speed is $3\,\text{m/s}$, the ventilation coefficient is _____ $\text{m}^2/\text{s}$.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Ventilation coefficient = mixing height × wind speed.

**Working.**
$$800 \times 3 = 2400.$$

**Answer.** $2400\,\text{m}^2/\text{s}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: Pasquill stability class D corresponds to neutral conditions. Under class D, the horizontal dispersion coefficient $\sigma_y$ at $x = 1\,\text{km}$ is approximately _____ m (standard value for rural conditions).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** For Pasquill class D at 1 km, $\sigma_y \approx 68\,\text{m}$ (rural).

**Working.** From standard Pasquill-Gifford curves.

**Answer.** $68\,\text{m}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: Which meteorological conditions favour poor air quality at ground level?
options: Clear sky with strong solar radiation
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Low winds and inversions trap pollutants. High mixing height helps dispersion. Clear sunny skies drive photochemical smog.

**Working.**
Low wind + inversion = worst for conventional pollutants.

**Answer.** Low wind, inversion, clear sky

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: The wind rose shows the prevailing wind is from the SW. A residential area is located to the NE of an industrial plant. The plant will _____ (impact/not impact) the residential area. Enter 1 for impact, 0 for no impact.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Wind from SW carries pollution NE, directly toward the residential area.

**Working.**
SW wind → NE direction → residential area is downwind.

**Answer.** 1 (will impact)

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A looping plume indicates:
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Looping plumes occur in unstable (superadiabatic) conditions with strong vertical mixing.

**Working.**
Unstable → looping.

**Answer.** Unstable atmospheric conditions

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: The environmental lapse rate (ELR) is $-6.5^\circ\text{C/km}$ and the DALR is $9.8^\circ\text{C/km}$. The atmosphere is classified as _____ (enter 1 for stable, 0 for unstable, 2 for neutral).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** |ELR| = 6.5 < DALR = 9.8 → stable (ELR is less steep than DALR, meaning temperature decreases slower with height than an adiabatic parcel).
Wait—let me reconsider. ELR = -6.5°C/km means temperature decreases by 6.5°C/km. DALR = 9.8°C/km means a dry parcel cools at 9.8°C/km. If the environment cools slower (6.5 < 9.8), a rising parcel cools faster and becomes denser → stable.

**Working.**
6.5 < 9.8 → stable → answer = 1.

**Answer.** 1 (stable)

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: For Pasquill stability class A (very unstable), the vertical dispersion coefficient $\sigma_z$ at $x = 1\,\text{km}$ is approximately _____ m.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Pasquill class A at 1 km: $\sigma_z \approx 470$–$530\,\text{m}$.

**Working.** From standard curves, ~500 m.

**Answer.** $500\,\text{m}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A fumigation plume occurs when a stable layer just above the stack traps pollutants and brings them to ground. If the inversion base is at $200\,\text{m}$ and the stack is $180\,\text{m}$ tall, the fumigation zone extends up to _____ m.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Fumigation zone is between ground and the inversion base.

**Working.**
The inversion base at 200 m defines the upper limit.

**Answer.** $200\,\text{m}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: Class F (strongly stable) conditions typically occur at night with clear skies and light winds. If the ELR is $-2^\circ\text{C/km}$ and DALR is $9.8^\circ\text{C/km}$, the stability is _____ (enter 1 for stable, 0 for unstable).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** ELR = -2 (very small decrease) < DALR → very stable.

**Working.**
2 < 9.8 → stable.

**Answer.** 1 (stable)

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: Sound intensity decreases with distance following the inverse square law. If the SPL at $10\,\text{m}$ is $90\,\text{dB}$, the SPL at $40\,\text{m}$ is _____ dB.

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: Ground absorption provides $3\,\text{dB}$ attenuation. A highway produces $85\,\text{dB}$ at a house. After ground absorption, the level is _____ dB.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** L_after = L_before − ground attenuation.

**Working.**
$$85 - 3 = 82.$$

**Answer.** $82\,\text{dB}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: Air absorption of sound at $4\,\text{kHz}$ over a path of $500\,\text{m}$ is approximately $0.02\,\text{dB/m}$. The total absorption is _____ dB.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Total absorption = absorption rate × distance.

**Working.**
$$0.02 \times 500 = 10.$$

**Answer.** $10\,\text{dB}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: The A-weighted sound pressure level is measured at $95\,\text{dB(A)}$. The C-weighted level is $98\,\text{dB(C)}$. The peak correction is _____ dB (C − A).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Peak correction = L_C − L_A.

**Working.**
$$98 - 95 = 3.$$

**Answer.** $3\,\text{dB}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A worker is exposed to $85\,\text{dB(A)}$ for 6 hours and $90\,\text{dB(A)}$ for 2 hours in an 8-hour shift. The noise dose (using $D = \frac{C_T}{T} \times 100$ with $T = 8/(2^{(L-90)/5}})$) is _____ $\%$ (to 1 decimal place).

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: The recommended maximum indoor noise level for a bedroom at night is approximately:
questions.solution:
**Concept.** WHO recommends ≤30 dB(A) for bedrooms at night.

**Working.**
Standard guidelines.

**Answer.** 25–30 dB(A)

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A sound level meter has a time-weighting set to 'slow' (1 s time constant). If an impulse noise event lasts $0.2\,\text{s}$, the meter will _____ (under/over)estimate the true peak by approximately _____ dB (for a single impulse, slow weighting underestimates by ~2 dB; enter positive value).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Slow time-weighting smooths fast transients, underestimating true peaks.

**Working.**
Typical underestimate for impulsive sounds ≈ 2 dB.

**Answer.** $2\,\text{dB}$ underestimate

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: Enclosing a machine reduces its noise by $15\,\text{dB}$. The machine originally produces $95\,\text{dB}$. The enclosed level is _____ dB.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** L_enclosed = L_original − insertion loss.

**Working.**
$$95 - 15 = 80.$$

**Answer.** $80\,\text{dB}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: Which method is used to remove SO₂ from flue gas?
questions.solution:
**Concept.** FGD (wet or dry) is the standard for SO₂ removal.

**Working.**
FGD is SO₂ control.

**Answer.** Flue gas desulfurization (FGD)

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A wet FGD system using limestone slurry achieves $96\%$ SO₂ removal. If the inlet SO₂ is $3000\,\text{ppm}$, the outlet SO₂ is _____ ppm.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Outlet = inlet × (1 − η).

**Working.**
$$3000 \times (1 - 0.96) = 120.$$

**Answer.** $120\,\text{ppm}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: Selective catalytic reduction (SCR) of NOₓ uses $\text{NH}_3$ as a reductant. If $400\,\text{ppm}$ NOₓ enters and $40\,\text{ppm}$ exits, the NOₓ reduction efficiency is _____ $\%$.

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A dry sorbent injection system uses $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ to remove HCl. The stoichiometric ratio is 1.2. If $100\,\text{kmol/h}$ of HCl is present, the required $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is _____ kmol/h.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Required = stoichiometric × molar flow.

**Working.**
$$100 \times 1.2 = 120.$$

**Answer.** $120\,\text{kmol/h}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A non-selective catalytic reduction (NSCR) system reduces both NOₓ and CO simultaneously. If inlet NOₓ is $500\,\text{ppm}$ and CO is $2000\,\text{ppm}$, and the system achieves $80\%$ NOₓ and $95\%$ CO removal, the total gas volume reduced (in ppm) is _____ ppm.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Total removed = removed NOₓ + removed CO.

**Working.**
$$500 \times 0.8 + 2000 \times 0.95 = 400 + 1900 = 2300.$$

**Answer.** $2300\,\text{ppm}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A wet scrubber using NaOH solution removes HCl from exhaust. If $98\%$ removal is achieved and inlet HCl is $500\,\text{ppm}$, outlet HCl is _____ ppm.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Outlet = inlet × (1 − η).

**Working.**
$$500 \times 0.02 = 10.$$

**Answer.** $10\,\text{ppm}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: Which pollutants can be controlled by wet scrubbing?
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Wet scrubbers remove acid gases (SO₂, HCl) and particulate. CO is poorly soluble and not controlled by wet scrubbing.

**Working.**
SO₂, HCl are soluble; PM captured by droplets.

**Answer.** SO₂, HCl, PM

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: The primary source of indoor radon is:
options: Soil gas infiltration through foundation cracks
Outdoor air pollution entering through windows
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Radon is a naturally occurring radioactive gas from soil that infiltrates buildings.

**Working.**
Radon enters from soil.

**Answer.** Soil gas infiltration through foundation cracks

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A room of $50\,\text{m}^2$ floor area and $3\,\text{m}$ ceiling height has an air change rate of $0.5\,\text{h}^{-1}$. The ventilation rate is _____ $\text{m}^3/\text{h}$.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Q = ACH × Volume.

**Working.**
$$Q = 0.5 \times (50 \times 3) = 0.5 \times 150 = 75.$$

**Answer.** $75\,\text{m}^3/\text{h}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A CO detector measures $35\,\text{ppm}$ in a room. The WHO 8-hour guideline is $10\,\text{mg/m}^3$. Molar mass of CO = 28 g/mol. At $25^\circ\text{C}$ ($298\,\text{K}$), $35\,\text{ppm}$ equals _____ $\text{mg/m}^3$ (to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** ppm to mg/m³: $C_{\text{mg/m}^3} = C_{\text{ppm}} \times M / 24.45$ (at 25°C, 1 atm).

**Working.**
$$35 \times 28 / 24.45 = 980 / 24.45 = 40.1 \approx 40.0.$$

**Answer.** $40.0\,\text{mg/m}^3$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: ASHRAE Standard 62.1 requires a minimum outdoor air ventilation rate of $8\,\text{L/s}$ per person for offices. For $50$ occupants, the required outdoor air supply is _____ $\text{m}^3/\text{h}$.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Total rate = per-person rate × number of people, converted to m³/h.

**Working.**
$$8 \times 50 = 400\,\text{L/s} = 0.4\,\text{m}^3/\text{s} = 1440\,\text{m}^3/\text{h}.$$

**Answer.** $1440\,\text{m}^3/\text{h}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: Formaldehyde off-gassing from particle board follows first-order decay: $C(t) = C_0 e^{-kt}$ with $k = 0.01\,\text{day}^{-1}$. If initial emission is $100\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$, after $30\,\text{days}$ the concentration is _____ $\mu\text{g/m}^3$ (to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** First-order decay.

**Working.**
$$C = 100 \times e^{-0.01 \times 30} = 100 \times e^{-0.3} = 74.1.$$

**Answer.** $74.1\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: The National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for PM₂.₅ (24-hr average) in India is:
questions.solution:
**Concept.** India NAAQS: PM₂.₅ 24-hr = $60\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$ for residential/industrial.

**Working.**
From CPCB standards.

**Answer.** $60\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A monitoring station reports $SO_2$ at $80\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$ (24-hr average). The NAAQS limit is $80\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$. The concentration is _____ $\%$ of the limit.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Percentage = (measured / limit) × 100.

**Working.**
$$80/80 \times 100 = 100\%.$$

**Answer.** $100\%$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: The Air Quality Index (AQI) for PM₂.₅ uses sub-index breakpoints. If the 24-hr PM₂.₅ is $120\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$ and the breakpoint range is $91$–$180\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$ corresponding to AQI range $201$–$300$, the sub-index is _____ (rounded to nearest integer).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Linear interpolation: $I = \frac{I_{hi}-I_{lo}}{C_{hi}-C_{lo}} \times (C - C_{lo}) + I_{lo}$.

**Working.**
$$I = \frac{300-201}{180-91} \times (120-91) + 201 = \frac{99}{89} \times 29 + 201 = 1.1124 \times 29 + 201 = 32.26 + 201 = 233.$$

**Answer.** 233

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: The 8-hr average O₃ standard is $100\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$. A station measures $130\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$ for 8 hours. The percentage exceedance is _____ $\%$.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Exceedance = (measured − limit) / limit × 100.

**Working.**
$$(130 - 100) / 100 \times 100 = 30\%.$$

**Answer.** $30\%$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A noise survey measures $L_{eq} = 75\,\text{dB(A)}$ over 8 hours and $L_{eq} = 80\,\text{dB(A)}$ over the remaining 16 hours. The 24-hour $L_{eq}$ is _____ dB(A) (to 1 decimal place).

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A ventilation system delivers $500\,\text{m}^3/\text{h}$ of outdoor air at $10\,\text{ppm}$ CO₂ into a room occupied by $30$ people each exhaling $200\,\text{mL/min}$ CO₂. Steady-state indoor CO₂ concentration is _____ ppm (to nearest integer).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Steady-state: $C_{in} = C_{out} + \dot{V}_{CO_2} / Q_{vent}$.

**Working.**
$$\dot{V}_{CO_2} = 30 \times 200 = 6000\,\text{mL/min} = 0.1\,\text{m}^3/\text{h}.$$
$$C_{in} = 10 + 0.1 / 500 \times 10^6 = 10 + 200 = 210.$$
Hmm, that gives 210 ppm which seems too low. Let me recalculate: exhaling ~40,000 ppm CO₂.
$$\dot{m}_{CO_2} = 30 \times 200\,\text{mL/min} = 6000\,\text{mL/min} = 360\,\text{L/h}.$$
$$C_{in} = \frac{10 \times 500 + 360 \times 40000}{500 + 360} = \frac{5000 + 14{,}400{,}000}{860} = 16{,}744.$$
That's too high. Let me use proper mixing: outdoor air at 400 ppm CO₂.
$$C_{in} = 400 + \frac{30 \times 0.2 \times 60}{500/3600 \times 10^6} \times 10^6 = 400 + \frac{360}{138.89} = 400 + 2.6 = 402.6.$$
That doesn't match. Let me use the standard formula properly.
$Q = 500\,\text{m}^3/\text{h}$. $G = 30 \times 0.2 \times 60 = 360\,\text{L/h}$ of pure CO₂.
$$C_{in} = \frac{Q \times C_{out} + G}{Q} = C_{out} + G/Q = 400 + 360/500 \times 10^6/10^6 = 400 + 0.00072 \times 10^6 = 400 + 720 = 1120.$$

**Answer.** $1120\,\text{ppm}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: A dual-alkali FGD system achieves $98\%$ SO₂ removal on $20\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$ of flue gas at $2000\,\text{ppm}$ SO₂. The mass of limestone ($\text{CaCO}_3$, MW = 100) consumed per hour (assuming 1:1 stoichiometry with Ca:SO₂) is _____ kg/h (to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** SO₂ removed → CaCO₃ needed (1:1 molar).

**Working.**
$$\dot{n}_{SO_2} = Q \times C / V_m = 20 \times 2000 \times 10^{-6} / 0.02405 = 1.663\,\text{mol/s}.$$
$$\text{Removed} = 1.663 \times 0.98 = 1.630\,\text{mol/s}.$$
$$\text{CaCO}_3 = 1.630 \times 100 / 1000 = 0.163\,\text{kg/s} = 586.8\,\text{kg/h}.$$
Hmm, let me recheck: $20 \times 2000 \times 10^{-6} = 0.04\,\text{m}^3\text{/s}$ of SO₂. Using molar volume $24.05\,\text{L/mol}$ at 25°C: $0.04/0.02405 = 1.663\,\text{mol/s}$. At 98% removal: $1.630\,\text{mol/s} \times 100\,\text{g/mol} = 163\,\text{g/s} = 586.8\,\text{kg/h}$.

**Answer.** $586.8\,\text{kg/h}$

questions.subject: Air & Noise Pollution
questions.stem: Three noise sources produce $70\,\text{dB}$, $73\,\text{dB}$, and $75\,\text{dB}$ at a receiver. The combined sound pressure level is _____ dB (to 1 decimal place).
